facts.text: I have pain in my belly.
It's all over my belly, not in one spot.
I feel tired all the time.
It has been getting steadily worse.
Some of the joints in my hands hurt.
The painful joints in my hands are swollen.

facts.item: hand joint pain and swelling: which joints
facts.text: It's the knuckles at the base of my index and middle fingers, on both hands.
My sex drive has been low.
It's been like that for about a year.
On both hands some fingers are badly pulled in towards the palm and won't straighten.
Both of my breasts have got bigger.
The skin on my face and hands, where the sun hits it, has gone darker.
Two years ago I was diagnosed with gout in my knees and ankles.
The treatment for it never really helped.
I have stage III high blood pressure, but it's well controlled.
I was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes.
I take metformin for the diabetes.
I don't use tobacco.
I haven't been exposed to any toxins.
I drink alcohol only occasionally.
There's nothing notable in my family's medical history.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: Hyperpigmentation of sun-exposed skin on the face and hands.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Mildly enlarged spleen; tenderness in the right upper quadrant.

findings.name: hand radiographs
findings.result: Juxta-articular osteopenia; large bony proliferations at the proximal interphalangeal joints; erosion of the fourth digit of the left hand; fixed flexion deformities.

findings.name: ultrasound of the hands
findings.result: Osteophytes with a step-up lesion; a large erosion in the right hand; signs of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate deposition.

findings.name: foot ultrasound
findings.result: Double-contour sign at the first metatarsal head, consistent with his gout history.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: Rheumatoid factor negative; anti-citrullinated protein antibodies negative.

findings.name: liver function tests
findings.result: Cholestatic enzymes (alkaline phosphatase, γ-glutamyl transferase) and total bilirubin approximately three times the upper limit of normal.

findings.name: abdominal ultrasound
findings.result: Hyperechoic, steatotic liver with nodularity, irregular margins and reduced vascular flow; no focal lesions; spleen 14 cm.

findings.name: FibroScan
findings.result: Stage III steatosis and grade IV fibrosis.

findings.name: upper endoscopy
findings.result: Mild gastritis and a Schatzki ring.

gold.reasoning: 1. Rheumatoid arthritis was considered given the painful polyarticular involvement, but it was excluded because “he displayed no increase in inflammatory markers, negative rheumatoid factor and anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPA).” 2. Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease was suggested by ultrasound findings but hand lesions represented destructive osteoarthritis with atypical distribution—“joint lesions were indicative of destructive osteoarthritis (OA) but with atypical distribution; thus, more tests were deemed necessary to confirm the diagnosis and etiology.” 3. Gout explained the forefoot findings but not the hand disease: “foot ultrasound indicated the presence of the double-contour sign at the first metatarsal, compatible with the patient’s previous diagnosis of gout.” 4. Dupuytren’s contracture could be secondary to alcohol, diabetes, or vitamin D deficiency, but risk factors were insufficient—“A bilateral Dupuytren’s contracture can occur due to alcohol consumption, diabetes or vitamin D deficiency and these could have partly explained the patient’s asthenia.”

notes: Index visit: the outpatient evaluation for diffuse abdominal pain, progressive fatigue and painful swelling of the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints (s001-s015); the low libido he admitted later in the evaluation (s006) predates it and is a fact.

Visible signs from the examination (Dupuytren's contracture, gynecomastia, skin darkening) are facts in lay words and stay in the examination findings; splenomegaly and right-upper-quadrant tenderness are examiner-only findings.
The pain and swelling of the hand joints share one joint location fact.
The gout diagnosis two years earlier is kept as current medical history (no resolution is stated).
